title: My Bibliography

My Bibliography

ORA video recording. Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SpFcC0eRk8Q
This is an AUTO-GENERATED transcript of the spoken narration, not an authored ORA document. Speech recognition can mis-hear names, dollar amounts and dates — check the recording before relying on a specific figure.

My Bibliography is one of the free tools available
to all My NCBI users. It lets you store, manage, and share PubMed
and manually-created citations. You can add PubMed citations right here in
My Bibliography or from the PubMed search page Select one or more citations to add, then use the Send to menu and Add to My Bibliography. That gives me this reassuring message, New
items were added to your bibliography. Now back in My Bib here is the newly added
citation. You can sort this list using the menu on the
right, and the citations added from PubMed are linked
to the PubMed abstract page. To add a non-PubMed citation, use the Add
citations menu and select Manually. Here you can add citations for items such
as books, presentations, patents, and datasets. In the Manage citations menu, you can export
your bibliography to a MEDLINE-formatted text file, which is handy if you want to import
your citations into an external reference manager. My Bibliography has additional features for
investigators funded through the NIH extramural program. When logged in and linked to eRA Commons,
you will see the eRA logo. Award view features will be covered in a separate
video. We'd love to have your feedback and questions. Please use the Support Center link found on
most NCBI web pages.
